resources.string: UTC determines the stellar epoch. Enter a WGS84 station; source SPK and IERS coverage is required. Catalog covariance is not propagated to the station direction.
Estimate refraction with explicit weather inputs
Airless apparent direction — azimuth north-zero, east-positive
Airless altitude is below 5°; no refracted result is supplied.
The solar-deflection limiter is active near the solar center.
Coordinate direction before aberration and deflection

Displayed digits do not establish physical accuracy. Altitude and solar elongation are not visibility judgments. Terrain, daylight, body disks, stellar size, direction covariance and event timing remain unmodeled. Refraction is only supplied at airless altitude at least 5°; local atmospheric accuracy is not certified. Export retains both original-source receipts.
Import original Gaia manifest and CSV. This is a uniform single-star model, not a ground apparent sky.
Adopt spectroscopic RV as astrometric RV; astrophysical shifts remain uncorrected.
Propagate formal covariance assuming RV errors are independent of astrometry.
Save stellar calculation and original sources
Select original files and explicit assumptions.
A source provider is still busy. Retry after it responds.

First-order covariance is optional. No systematics, binary acceleration or observer corrections. Standard deviations are not joint confidence regions or occultation timing guarantees. Full sources, matrices and assumptions are retained in the export.

Import original SBDB cov=mat JSON requested with full-prec=1. Convert at the covariance solution epoch in the heliocentric IAU76/80 J2000 ecliptic frame. Supply an explicit solar GM and its source; no constant is assumed.
Nominal coordinates and formal marginal standard deviations

First-order coordinate conversion only; no future propagation or event probability. Full joint covariance, including extra parameters and cross terms, is retained in the export. Source binding does not independently validate the numerical result, authenticate the source, or prove physical accuracy.

Requires the pinned DE440 source installed on the backend. Enter the original covariance solution epoch and a signed duration of at most 365 days. Only six-parameter sources are supported. The adopted solar GM comes from the pinned DE440 file.
Elapsed TDB seconds (negative for backward propagation)
Adopt the restricted DE440 force model and its fixed parameters

Supply each exclusion distance explicitly. These limits stop a run at force evaluations; they are not continuous collision detection. Earth and Moon are separate; other planets use system barycenters.
Include constant unshadowed radial radiation pressure
Fixed effective area, mass, optical coefficient and solar pressure. No shadow, attitude, variable flux, outgassing or uncertainty in these parameters is modelled.
Final heliocentric IAU76/80 J2000 ecliptic coordinates and formal marginal standard deviations
SBDB source-fit PE / SB: %1$s / %2$s · Adopted integration kernel: %3$s. Identifier comparison does not establish fit-model equivalence.

Conditional first-order covariance under the adopted fixed-parameter model, not the complete SBDB orbit-fit uncertainty or an event probability. No ephemeris, GM or SRP parameter uncertainty is included. Source/receipt consistency is not independent accuracy verification. The export retains original source bytes, force settings, numerical diagnostics, transition matrix and covariance square root.
Maximum accepted local error ratio: %1$s · Relative tolerance: %2$s

The ratio is the maximum component-normalized embedded local error estimate across accepted steps, not a global error bound, source uncertainty or physical accuracy. Absolute tolerances and state-transition layout are retained in the export. Zero duration has no accepted steps; zero diagnostics do not establish accuracy.
Integrate again to compare covariance with tighter tolerances

The comparison uses one-tenth tolerances and half initial/maximum steps under the same 20-second backend deadline. Same-model differences are not independent validation, global error bounds or physical uncertainty. Zero-duration agreement supplies no convergence evidence. Export retains both full results.
Refined endpoint · formal σ · absolute σ difference from baseline

Supply a flat JSON array in the original SBDB covariance label order and units: six offsets per draw, 1 to 128 draws. These are caller-supplied offsets, not automatically generated probability samples. Both source and offsets are retained in the export.
Source offsets (JSON array, at most 32768 characters)
Enter 1 to 128 complete six-axis draws as finite JSON numbers.
Descriptive endpoint mean · sample standard deviation

Adopted force model and sources · checked receipt values, not independent source authentication. Integration frame below differs from the heliocentric endpoint frame. Exclusion distances are not continuous collision detection.
Full sample covariance · divisor %1$d. Entry units are row units multiplied by column units. Finite-batch descriptive statistics, not confidence regions or physical error bounds.
Moments unavailable because at least one draw failed; successful draws are not silently substituted.
Moments unavailable: at least two draws are required.

Heliocentric IAU76/80 J2000 ecliptic endpoints under fixed adopted forces. All draws share the backend 20-second context and 250000 force-evaluation budget. No extra fitted force axes, continuous collision detection, calibrated event probabilities or physical error bounds. Zero-duration agreement is not convergence evidence. Receipt checks are consistency checks, not independent numerical validation. Export retains full integration diagnostics and covariance statistics.
